properties.decision: Recorded as brainstorming, not as a proposal. From the hxm_program session's first-ranked cause, relayed by Anthony on 2026-09-14: the where-am-i skill "triggers on the user asking where things stand, or picking a design back up after a break. You asked me to build a deck for management. I never mapped 'produce a progress deck' onto 'read the design first'. A clause saying the audience is not the trigger would have caught it outright, and that is the cheapest fix on the list." Options as they stand: (a) the cheap one — add the clause to the skill's trigger text and to the nudge string, so the trigger names the ACT of asserting status whoever the audience is; (b) the structural one — find or add a tool call that marks "about to assert status" the way record_finding marks "about to write a cause", and demand the skill from that tool; (c) accept that this trigger is internal state, like root-cause's, and rely on (a) plus the measured load rate.
properties.name: OPEN — should the orientation skill trigger on the agent being about to ASSERT status for anyone (a deck, a report, a summary, a claim of what was achieved), not only on the user asking where things stand — and can any served tool mark that moment?
properties.rationale: Why it is not simply (a): the design already measured that a trigger keyed on the agent's own internal state, with no tool call to hang a demand on, loads only by luck (19 to 24 percent). "About to assert status" is a second member of that class. Option (a) is cheap and was judged by the reporting session to have caught this instance; whether it would have caught the earlier occurrences is the test step 6 of the root-cause skill asks, and it has not been run.
